title: Grateful Dead Live at Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke U on 1973-12-08
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v3 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1973 show with a stellar Weather Report Suite and other epic jams captured on a mostly solid soundboard recording (some mix quirks).
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the blazing Weather Report Suite, a tight China Cat > Rider sequence, and an out‑of‑this‑world The Other One that veers into dark, space‑y territory. The soundboard source is generally clear and vibrant, though a few reviewers note occasional drum dropouts and a brief “Johnny B” glitch. Overall the performance ranks among the best of the fall ’73 tour.

ai_rating.rationale: 13 reviews, 11 of them 5‑star and only one low (3‑star) comment; praise for both musical performance and recording outweighs the few technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mostly crisp, well‑balanced soundboard with excellent instrument separation. Minor issues: a drop of "Johnny B" in the first set, occasional drum mix weakness (some reviewers hear missing drums), and a brief glitch noted by one user.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A sprawling 16‑song first set builds a light, funky groove that feeds into an even more adventurous second set. The sequence from Wharf Rat through Stella is oddly paced but leads into the legendary Other One jam; overall pacing is praised for its energy and daring transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar leads are described as climatic (Weather Report Suite) and his vocals ‘extra sweet’ and full of emotion, especially on ballads and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: A notable Phil bass “splurge” in the Rider solo is highlighted; deep, resonant dissonances in the space jam are likened to Phil & Ned moments.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby McGee receives high praise as possibly the best of ’73; Bob’s rhythm work is mentioned as hot and driving throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboard work shines – Dragnet tease, excellent playing on They Love Each Other, and a standout solo in Rider; overall keys are praised for adding funkiness.
band_member_comments.Drums: Generally solid Bill Kreutzmann drumming, though one reviewer notes the mix sometimes drowns out drums early in the show.
